items.problem: CS0104 'HttpMethod' / 'HttpCompletionOption' is an ambiguous reference between System.Net.Http and Windows.Web.Http (Scenario3_RequestModification.xaml.cs:323/326).
items.evidence: migration-score.json candidate_build_errors[1] and [2]; source files use 'using Windows.Web.Http;' plus 'using Windows.Web.Http.Filters;' (session-log.txt L467-468, L1818-1820) and call HttpRequestMessage / HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead (L7709/L7712).
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Common build errors' -> '### CS0104: "LaunchActivatedEventArgs" is an ambiguous reference', whose closing line generalizes 'The same pattern applies to any other type name that exists in both Windows.UI.Xaml.* and Microsoft.UI.Xaml.* namespaces'.
items.proposed_improvement: Broaden the existing CS0104 section so it is not framed as a Windows.UI.Xaml-only problem. Add a second, named collision axis: System.Net.Http (BCL, referenced by default in WinUI3 desktop) vs Windows.Web.Http (the WinRT stack UWP apps use). List the colliding type names (HttpClient, HttpMethod, HttpRequestMessage, HttpResponseMessage, HttpCompletionOption) and the resolution: keep Windows.Web.Http when the code relies on its IHttpFilter/HttpBaseProtocolFilter surface (which System.Net.Http has no equivalent for), and drop/alias the System.Net.Http using or fully-qualify the WinRT types.
items.generalizes: The System.Net.Http vs Windows.Web.Http collision hits any UWP app that performs HTTP networking with the WinRT stack — a common pattern across SDK samples (request modification, custom filters, headers). The current CS0104 guidance only mentions the Xaml axis, so agents do not connect it to the Http collision.
